name: Resource Ownership and Deterministic Teardown
description: Every resource (database connection, file handle, network socket, child process) has an owner. Teardown is ordered and deterministic.
purpose: No resource leaks, no dangling state.
acceptanceCriteria: Every resource is registered in a global resource registry with owner, type, and lifecycle scope
Resource teardown follows reverse order of acquisition (stack semantics)
Resource registry provides a dump of all live resources for leak detection
Teardown of one scope does not orphan resources in a child scope
Force-teardown after timeout logs warnings but never hangs the shutdown sequence
Resource registry is itself a resource with deterministic teardown (last in, first out)
required_evidence: Resource registry registration test (owner, type, lifecycle scope)
Scope teardown does not orphan child resources test
Resource registry self-teardown test (last in, first out)
acceptance_gates: Every resource registered with owner, type, scope
Scope teardown does not orphan child resources
rollback_strategy: Resource acquisition that fails mid-sequence triggers reverse-order teardown of already-acquired resources
recovery_strategy: On crash, resource registry is rebuilt from persistent resource journal; orphaned resources are cleaned up
escalation_policy: Resource leak detection exceeding threshold escalates to user with leak report
